note: Added 2026-09-09 together with 13 sibling Greater Vancouver property tax notices, on request, to grow `propertytax` coverage from 6 documents to 20. A 2026 ADVANCE tax notice from the City of Vancouver, not an annual levy: 'This Advance Tax Notice levy represents 50% of the net previous year's taxes', so it carries NO home owner grant columns and has a February due date. It is the second Vancouver document in the corpus and earns its place because it prints the same 'Property Tax Office' return-address header that defeats the vendor extract twin on property_vancouver -- here both twins read 'CITY OF VANCOUVER' 3/3 and the vendor resolves with no repair, so this is the control for propertytax_vendor_rescue rather than a case of it. invoice_date IS asserted: the page prints 'Statement Date: Dec 10, 2025'. payment_due_date from 'DUE DATE: Tuesday, February 3, 2026'. account_number is the printed folio 830-170-40-0125. || invoice_description NOT asserted: free-text that rewords itself every run. || The narrative fields (diagnosis_solution, recommendation, warranty and their zh_hant twins) are blank by policy on a municipal bill. || folio_number ADDED 2026-09-09 with the new folio twins (commercial-narrative-v20). It is a critical field on property tax notices only (field_policy.PROPERTYTAX_DELTA), and is asserted on every sidecar -- the value on a tax notice, "" everywhere else -- so a regression that starts populating it on ordinary invoices is caught. || number_of_days ASSERTION REMOVED 2026-09-09 (user authorised, all 20 property_* sidecars): the Power Automate flow does not consume number_of_days for property tax. It was removed from the whole family rather than only where it flakes, so the tax notices stay uniform. Behaviour seen: the period resolves 2026-01-01..2026-12-31 on every read (365 days inclusive), number_of_days_extract returns no value at all, and number_of_days_generate intermittently invents '1' -- catalogued defect B3 -- which reconcile_number_of_days then corrects to 365, while an empty twin pair stays blank by that function's explicit 'corrects only; never supplies' design. The field therefore flipped '' <-> 365 between runs. || billing_period_start_date AND billing_period_end_date ASSERTIONS REMOVED 2026-09-09 (user authorised, all 20 propertytax sidecars): the Power Automate flow does not consume the billing period for property tax, so the corpus no longer asserts it on this family. Both fields REMAIN in WRITE_FIELDS and still reach Dynamics -- removing the assertion stops the corpus checking them, it does not stop them being written. What this gives up, stated once: on the 16 notices that asserted '' the pair was the guard against a generate twin inventing a period out of nothing, and on property_surrey it was catching a real failure chain -- B3's invented number_of_days=1 makes the code derive start = end - 1 day, which collapses the period to zero length and blanks a correct 2026-01-01 (open-defects A13b, measured 4 of 6 reads correct). That chain is unfixed and is now invisible to the corpus on every property tax notice. || account_number is written WITHOUT the 'Account No: ' prefix on this family (user requirement, 2026-09-09, propertytax ONLY -- every other municipal bill and every commercial invoice keeps the label). The written value is the bare folio, which is what an owner quotes to the municipality. || RAW-READING ASSERTIONS REMOVED 2026-09-14 (user authorised, all 54 sidecars): the corpus checks only written values (writeValues) and routingDecision, never a raw CU extract/generate reading. Removed here: total_invoice_amount_extract, total_invoice_amount_generate, sub_bill_type, sub_bill_type_generate.
